summary: A two-storey white-concrete beach house on a 42x18x38 sand-and-sea site, built as code in three stages (`make.sh`). Stage 1 is massing: an offset lower and upper box, the upper cantilevered east and south on slim quartz pillars. Stage 2 is the roof from `mcd roof --spec roof.json` (cafe preset with a dark graphite palette, dry-run clean, no warnings). Stage 3 is the finish: glazing, doors, entry, deck, pool, props and site. `mcd check` shows 0 floating blocks and 0 unsupported attachments; the 46 orphans reported are all palm-frond leaf tips. `mcd palette` flags only white-on-white wool in the parasol stripes. `build.nbt`, `elements.md`, `tasks.json` (10 tasks) and `gaps.md` are saved.
elements: Flat cantilevered roof plate with deep eaves: `mcd roof` cafe preset (flat deck, quartz fascia, birch soffit) with a dark polished-deepslate/deepslate-tile/blackstone mix, never hand-placed
Stacked offset white volumes: white_concrete boxes with a gray_concrete datum ring at each floor; upper volume cantilevered over the deck and the east carport on 5 quartz_pillar columns

Floor-to-ceiling glazing: light_blue_stained_glass_pane in white frames on the south wall, ribbon window on the north, corner glazing on the east, with real birch double doors to deck, carport and roof terrace
Recessed entry porch: wall omitted by exclusion, birch door, two hanging lanterns, stone stepping path, stair up, glowing '12' / 'DUNE WALK' wall signs on a dark panel
Timber slat privacy screen: open birch trapdoors as vertical fins between stripped birch log posts, with a slab beam and a dune-grass garden and azaleas behind
Birch plank sun deck with a tinted-pane glass balustrade, steps to the sand, and a jetty with fence posts and a lantern into the sea
Plunge pool: sealed water source cells flush with the deck, in a smooth_quartz coping ring with a light_blue_concrete floor
Sun loungers (quartz stairs + slabs + carpet towels) and striped parasols (fence pole, orange/cyan wool canopy)

Carport terrace: smooth_stone floor, campfire fire pit in a stone-brick slab ring with quartz-stair benches, hanging lanterns, 4 surfboards as stacked wall banners with stripe and border patterns, flowering azalea planter
Roof terrace over the lower volume: birch deck, tinted pane balustrade, azalea planter box, loungers
Beach: sand with a sinuous waterline of water blocks, wet smooth_sandstone edge, boulders from `boulder()`, hand-built jungle-log palms, grass_block dune-grass tufts with short_grass/dead_bush
Interior seen through the glass: quartz sofa, rug, kitchen island with trapdoor stools, birch stair flight, bed, bookshelf wall
polish: Glazing renders near-black because the renderer has no light engine, so the big glass walls read as dark voids, though the through-views to the sky read as glass; the black datum ring and the glass sit close in tone.
Palms are hand-built with a blocky trunk jog and drooping leaf tips (the check's orphan list); they read as palms but are not elegant, and the NW palm hides part of the carport from the street.
The surfboards (stacked wall banners on the carport side) are small and mostly hidden from the street, so they barely read as boards; the rack posts were dropped and are still a task.
The house-number signs are tiny on a dark panel and unreadable at the glance scale.
The exposed lower-roof terrace is a hand-set deck, not a preset roof, because `mcd roof` takes one eave height; the cafe roof's fascia is only on the upper volume.
The roof plate is a flat dark slab with no rooftop interest; solar panels did not fit the roof slab geometry.
The sea is a thin strip at the grid edge with no waves or foam, the sand is one flat colour, and the deck is a single plain birch field with no board rhythm.
Interior furnishing is sparse and mostly invisible from outside. The glass balustrade is nearly invisible at street distance.
